div.head: Af 42
div.ab: XXXVIII. Eac we beodað: se mon se ðe his gefán hamsittende wite, ðæt he ne feohte, ær ðam ðe he him ryhtes bidde.
XXXVIII. Eac we beodað: se mon se ðe his gefan hamsittendne wite, þæt he ne feohte, ær ðam he him ryhtes bidde.
Etiam instituimus: homo, qui inimicum suum residentem scit, non ante impugnet eum, quam sibi rectum postulet.
{XXXVIII} Eac we beodæð: se mon se ðe his gefán hamsittendne wite, þæt he ne feohte, ærðam he him ryhtes bidde.
Likewise we command: for the man who knows that his enemy is sitting at home, that he not fight him before he offers to settle according to law.
Also we enjoin, that a man who knows his adversary to be residing at home, shall not have recourse to violence before demanding justice of him.
Moreover we command: that the man who knows his opponent to be dwelling at home is not to fight before he asks justice for himself.
Auch gebieten wir: Jemand, der seinen [mit Racherecht zu verfolgenden] Feind als auf [eigenem] Hofe sitzend kennt, dass er nicht [in Rache] fechte, bevor er sich Recht [im Sühnewege] fordere.
We also command: someone who knows his [feud-]enemy to be sitting at home [on his own estate] is not to fight [in vengeance] before he demands justice for himself [by way of settlement].
div.note: A man against whom he has a legitimate blood-feud.
